html:
Three fantasy films directed by the New Zealander Peter Jackson and released from 2001 to 2003, based on the novel by J. R. R. Tolkien. They were made entirely in New Zealand and changed its film industry and its image abroad.

Jackson persuaded the American studio New Line Cinema to film all three parts at once. Shooting took well over a year across mountains, rivers and farmland in both islands of New Zealand. The effects and props were made in Wellington by Weta, which grew into a world leader in digital effects.

The films were a huge success, earning close to three billion dollars. The last, The Return of the King, won all eleven Oscars it was nominated for, tying the record.

New Zealand marketed itself as "the home of Middle-earth", and tourists came to see the filming sites, such as the hobbit village kept at a farm near Matamata. Wellington became a centre of film making. The films also gave a nickname, "the hobbit", to Homo floresiensis, announced in 2004.
sum: Three fantasy films directed by the New Zealander Peter Jackson and released from 2001 to 2003, based on the novel by J. R. R. Tolkien. They were made entirely in New Zealand and changed its film industry and its image abroad.
